recipes.title: Classic Hummus
recipes.description: The dish everything else is measured against. The texture comes from baking soda in the soak and the pot, not from a stronger blender.
instructions: Soak the chickpeas overnight in water with half the baking soda. They should double in size.

Drain, cover with fresh water and the remaining soda, and simmer 1.5-2 hours, until a chickpea crushes between two fingers with no resistance at all. A chickpea that still resists gives grainy hummus, and that is the usual mistake.
Skim the foam and floating skins as it cooks. There is no need to peel by hand.
Blend the chickpeas hot with the garlic and lemon to a smooth paste.
Add tahini, cumin and salt, and drizzle in ice water while blending until the mixture turns pale and airy.
Serve in a shallow plate, sweep a well with the back of a spoon and pour olive oil in. Parve - serve with hot pita.

recipes.title: Masabacha
recipes.description: The opposite of smooth hummus: the chickpeas stay whole and hot and the tahini is poured over them. The hummusiya breakfast.
instructions: Soak overnight and simmer about two hours with the soda, until the chickpeas are completely soft but still whole.
Keep a cup of the cooking liquid - it is what makes the sauce.
Make the tahini sauce: tahini, lemon, garlic, salt and hot cooking liquid, stirred to the consistency of pouring cream.
Crush about a quarter of the chickpeas into the sauce and leave the rest whole.
Serve hot, not at room temperature - that is the difference between masabacha and cold hummus.
Scatter parsley and paprika and pour olive oil over. Parve.

recipes.title: Falafel
recipes.description: Soaked chickpeas, never cooked ones - that is the whole lesson. A cooked chickpea falls apart in the oil and turns to paste.
instructions: Soak the chickpeas 12-24 hours. They are never cooked at any stage - that is what separates falafel from a chickpea patty.
Dry them well and grind with the onion, herbs and garlic in a meat grinder or strong blender, to a coarse crumb and not a paste.
Season with cumin, ground coriander, salt and pepper, and chill the mixture for an hour - it firms up in the cold.
Add the baking powder only just before frying. Any earlier and it loses its lift.
Heat the oil to 170C. Oil that is too hot burns the outside and leaves the middle raw.
Fry 3-4 minutes to a deep brown and drain. Serve in pita with tahini and salad. Parve.

recipes.title: Hummus with Fava
recipes.description: Smooth hummus under a layer of hot seasoned fava beans. Not the Egyptian breakfast - this is a topping spread over hummus.
instructions: Soak the fava overnight and simmer about an hour and a half until soft and easily crushed.
Crush about a third in the pot and leave the rest whole, so a thick sauce forms around the beans.
Season with crushed garlic, cumin, lemon, salt and chopped chilli. Season while hot - cold fava absorbs nothing.
Spread a layer of hummus on a plate and sweep a wide well in it.
Pour the hot fava into the centre and pour olive oil generously over.
Scatter parsley. Parve - served with raw onion and pita.

recipes.title: Hummus with Mushrooms
recipes.description: A Tel Aviv invention from the nineties. Mushrooms seared with soy and garlic over hummus - entirely parve, which is why it caught on.
instructions: Cut the mushrooms into thick slices. Thin ones disappear in the pan.
Heat a wide pan over high heat and sear in small batches - crowded mushrooms stew in their own water instead of browning.
Add the garlic and cook only half a minute, to the smell and not to the colour.
Deglaze with the wine, let it evaporate, then add soy and pepper.
Spread hummus on a plate and pour the hot mushrooms over with all their liquid.
Scatter parsley. Parve - the soy and wine must both be certified.

recipes.title: Hummus with Egg and Onion
recipes.description: A brown egg cooked for seven hours, sharp red onion and hummus. The Friday morning plate.
instructions: Cook the eggs in water with the onion skins on the lowest flame for at least an hour - they take on an amber colour and a faintly sweet taste. This is a hamin egg; without the skins it is only a hard-boiled one.
Cool in cold water and peel.
Slice the red onion into thin rings, salt lightly and rub between your fingers until it softens.
Toss the onion with sumac, lemon and olive oil.
Spread the hummus, halve the eggs over it and scatter the onion on top.
Drizzle olive oil and scatter parsley. Parve - an egg is neither meat nor dairy.

recipes.title: Hummus with Beef
recipes.description: Beef cooked until it collapses, in a thick sauce over hummus. The dish that turned hummus from breakfast into a meal.
instructions: Cut the beef into 2cm cubes and dry them on a towel. Wet meat will not brown.
Sear in small batches in hot olive oil until deeply crusted on all sides.
Remove, fry chopped onion in the same pot until golden, and add the tomato paste for a minute.
Return the meat, season with baharat, bay and salt, cover with water and simmer two hours on low heat until it falls apart under a fork.
Reduce the sauce uncovered until it coats a spoon.
Spread hummus, pour the meat and sauce into the centre and scatter pine nuts. Meat - there is not a drop of dairy in it.

recipes.title: Hummus with Shawarma
recipes.description: Turkey shawarma in a pan, no rotating spit. What is sold on every high street in Israel.
instructions: Toss the turkey slices with baharat, turmeric, cardamom, salt and oil and leave half an hour.
Heat an iron pan very hot and lay the slices in a single layer without stirring, a minute and a half each side - the edges must char.
Add thinly sliced onion and toss together three minutes more.
Make a tahini sauce with lemon and water - no yogurt, so it stays meat.
Spread hummus on a plate, pile the hot shawarma on and drizzle tahini over.
Serve with pickles, amba and pita. Meat.

recipes.title: Tahini Sauce
recipes.description: Three ingredients, and everyone fails it once: tahini seizes when you add water, and only then loosens.
instructions: Stir the tahini, lemon, garlic and salt together in a bowl.
Add the water gradually. The mixture will split and seize into a stiff lump - this is normal and not a failure, and this is where most people throw it out.
Keep whisking. After half a minute it breaks back into a smooth pale sauce.
Add water a spoon at a time to the texture you want: thick for spreading, looser for pouring over shawarma.
Correct salt and lemon. Tahini always needs more salt than it seems.
Scatter cumin and parsley and drizzle olive oil. Parve - which is why it accompanies both meat and fish.

recipes.title: Green Tahini
recipes.description: A whole bunch of parsley into the tahini. It stays green only if everything is cold and the blending is short.
instructions: Wash the herbs and dry them completely. Water on the leaves thins the sauce and dulls the colour.
Chop roughly and blend with lemon, garlic, chilli and salt.
Add the tahini and pulse only in short bursts - a blender left running heats the leaves and the green turns khaki.
Add ice water gradually to a pouring consistency.
Taste; if it is bitter it needs lemon, not salt.
Serve at once or keep refrigerated up to two days. Parve - it goes with fish, roasted vegetables and falafel.

recipes.title: Israeli Salad
recipes.description: The only difficulty is the knife. Half-centimetre dice, no food processor, no salt until the last moment.
instructions: Dice the cucumbers to half a centimetre. This is not decoration - a large cube separates the vegetables instead of mixing them.
Halve the tomatoes, scoop out the seeds and jelly and discard them. That liquid is what turns a salad into soup after ten minutes.
Chop the onion very fine and soak it a minute in the lemon juice to take the edge off.
Chop the herbs with a sharp knife, not scissors - a blunt blade bruises and blackens them.
Toss everything with olive oil and salt only at the table. Early salt draws water out of the cucumber.
Serve at once. Parve - which is why it reaches every table, meat or dairy.

recipes.title: Home-Baked Pita
recipes.description: The pocket opens from steam, not from yeast. A scorching oven and thin dough - there is no third way.
instructions: Mix the yeast, sugar and water and wait ten minutes for foam. No foam means dead yeast and dough that will not rise.
Knead with the flour, salt and oil for eight minutes, to a smooth dough that stretches without tearing.
Prove an hour until doubled, divide into eight balls and rest twenty minutes more, covered - dough that has dried out will not puff.
Heat the oven to 250C with a tray or stone already inside. A lukewarm oven gives a flatbread, not a pita.
Roll each ball to a 4-5mm round, no thinner, and lay it on the scorching tray.
Bake 4-6 minutes. The pita balloons and then collapses - that is the sign the pocket has formed. Parve.

recipes.title: Laffa
recipes.description: A soft flatbread made to wrap around shawarma. Cooked on a dry pan - no pocket, no oven.
instructions: Knead a soft, oily dough - it should be stickier than pita dough, and that is what keeps it pliable as it cools.
Prove an hour, divide into six and rest twenty minutes.
Roll very thin, almost translucent, to a 30cm round. A thick laffa stiffens within minutes.
Heat an iron pan or an upturned saj over high heat, with no oil at all.
Cook one minute on the first side until brown spots appear, then turn for only half a minute.
Move straight onto a kitchen towel and cover - the trapped steam is what keeps it soft. Parve.

recipes.title: Whole Roast Cauliflower with Tahini
recipes.description: The newest Israeli dish on this site - born in Tel Aviv after 2010 and copied worldwide.
instructions: Trim the stem so it sits flat and remove only the outer leaves. It stays whole.
Blanch it eight minutes in heavily salted boiling water, head down. This cooks the inside before the outside burns.
Dry it thoroughly - a wet cauliflower steams in the oven instead of browning.
Rub olive oil and coarse salt into every crevice and roast at 200C for about an hour, to a deep brown crust.
Make a thick tahini sauce with lemon, garlic and cold water.
Serve whole on a bed of the tahini, scatter sumac and nuts, and break it apart with a spoon at the table. Parve.

recipes.title: Burnt Aubergine Salad with Mayonnaise
recipes.description: Charred aubergine and mayonnaise - a pairing born in Israel and nowhere else. Mayonnaise is egg and oil, so it is parve.
instructions: Char the aubergines directly over an open flame until the skin is entirely black and they collapse, about 15 minutes. An oven gives a cooked aubergine with no smoke in it.
Put them in a covered bowl for ten minutes - the steam loosens the skin.
Peel and drain in a sieve for half an hour. An undrained aubergine turns the salad to liquid within the hour.
Chop with a knife, not a processor. A processor makes grey puree of it.
Mix with finely chopped onion, garlic, lemon, salt and pepper, and fold the mayonnaise in only at the end.
Chill an hour before serving. Parve - the mayonnaise must be free of dairy.

recipes.title: Aubergine with Tahini
recipes.description: The same charred aubergine, this time with tahini instead of mayonnaise - the version that comes to the table beside the meat.
instructions: Char the aubergines over an open flame until the skin is black and the flesh entirely soft.
Peel and drain half an hour. Keep the long strands rather than chopping fine - the texture is half the dish.
Make a thick tahini: tahini, lemon, garlic, salt and cold water added gradually until smooth.
Fold the aubergine into the tahini with a light hand and few strokes.
Correct lemon and salt. Tahini mutes salt, so it needs more than it seems.
Scatter pomegranate seeds and mint and pour olive oil over. Parve.

recipes.title: Home-Pickled Cucumbers
recipes.description: Cucumbers in a salt ferment, with no vinegar. Five days on the counter and the jar does the work itself.
instructions: Wash the cucumbers and trim a millimetre off the blossom end - the enzyme there softens pickles, and without it they stay crisp.
Boil the water with the salt, stir until dissolved and cool completely. Warm brine cooks the cucumber.
Pack a clean jar tightly with the cucumbers, layering in the garlic, dill, chillies and grape leaves.
Pour the brine over to cover completely and weigh them down - a cucumber floating above the liquid will mould.
Leave on the counter 4-6 days. The water clouds and the liquid bubbles - that is fermentation, not spoilage.
Move to the fridge when sour enough. Parve - they keep a month.

recipes.title: Falafel-Stand Cabbage Salad
recipes.description: White cabbage shaved paper-thin in vinegar and oil. What fills the bottom half of the pita at every stand in the country.
instructions: Shave the cabbage as thin as possible, on a mandoline or with a long knife. A thick slice will not take up the dressing.
Salt it and rub with your hands for a full minute until it softens and gives up water.
Squeeze the water out and throw it away. This is the step that turns a watery salad into one that keeps two days.
Grate the carrot on the coarse side and add it.
Whisk the vinegar, oil, sugar and caraway and pour over the cabbage.
Rest half an hour before serving. Parve - the vinegar must be certified.

recipes.title: Cheese Bourekas
recipes.description: The shape declares the filling - triangle for cheese, round for potato. A code set in Israeli bakeries and kept ever since.
instructions: Crumble the Bulgarian cheese and mix with the ricotta, one egg, dill and pepper. No salt - the cheese is salty enough.
Roll the pastry to 3mm and cut 10cm squares.
Put a spoon of filling in the centre, fold to a triangle and seal with fork tines. An open boureka loses all its filling in the oven.
Arrange on baking paper with space between them - puff pastry spreads as it rises.
Brush with beaten yolk and scatter sesame generously.
Bake at 200C for 25-30 minutes to a deep gold. Dairy - served with a hard-boiled egg and pickles.

recipes.title: Roasted Beetroot with Tahini
recipes.description: Beetroot roasted, not boiled - the oven concentrates the sweetness instead of washing it into the water.
instructions: Wrap each beetroot in foil with a little salt and oil and roast at 200C for about an hour, until a knife goes in without resistance.
Roast, do not boil - a beetroot cooked in water loses its colour and flavour into the pot.
Peel while still warm; the skin slips off in your hand.
Cut into 1cm dice and season with lemon, salt and olive oil while still hot.
Make a loose tahini sauce and drizzle it over without stirring - the contrast of white against purple is part of the dish.
Scatter chopped walnuts and coriander and trickle date syrup over. Parve.

recipes.title: Jerusalem Mixed Grill
recipes.description: Born at the Mahane Yehuda market from the cuts the butchers could not sell. The plancha must be scorching and never crowded.
instructions: The liver must be broiled over an open flame until its colour has changed all through, then rinsed. This is a kashrut requirement, not a preference, and without it the dish is not kosher.
Cut everything into strips of roughly the same size so they finish together.
Fry sliced onion in oil over medium heat for a full twenty minutes, to a deep sweet brown. This is the base.
Raise the heat high and add the hearts and spleen - they are the toughest and need the longest.
After five minutes add the breast, and the liver last of all; added early it dries out in moments.
Season with baharat, cumin, turmeric and salt, toss a minute and serve in pita with pickles. Meat.

recipes.title: Chicken Thigh Skewers
recipes.description: Thigh, never breast. The cut that carries enough fat to survive coals without drying.
instructions: Cut the thighs into 4cm cubes. Smaller than that and they dry out over the coals.
Mix a marinade of oil, paprika, garlic, cumin and pepper, without the salt and lemon.
Marinate in the fridge two hours to overnight. The lemon and salt go in only half an hour before grilling - acid over a long time "cooks" the meat and turns it mealy.
Thread tightly onto skewers so the cubes touch; that is what keeps the inside juicy.
Grill over hot coals four minutes a side. Turn once and no more.
Rest five minutes covered before serving, and scatter parsley. Meat.

recipes.title: Grilled Kebab
recipes.description: Lamb fat is what holds a kebab on the skewer. Lean meat falls into the coals - that is not folklore.
instructions: The mixture needs at least 20 percent fat. Too lean a grind will not hold on the skewer under any seasoning.
Grate the onion and squeeze every drop of liquid out of it by hand. Wet onion is the first cause of a kebab that falls apart.
Knead the meat with the onion, parsley, spices and matzah meal for a full five minutes, until the mixture turns sticky and pulls in threads.
Chill an hour. A cold mixture clings to the skewer; one at room temperature slides off.
Wet your hands and shape a cylinder around a flat skewer with even pressure and no air pockets.
Grill over medium-hot coals 5-6 minutes in total, turning once. Meat.

recipes.title: Oven Turkey Shawarma
recipes.description: Turkey breast layered with lamb fat on an improvised vertical spit. In Israel shawarma means turkey, not lamb.
instructions: Slice the turkey half a centimetre thick and marinate overnight in the spices, oil, lemon and grated onion.
Thread onto a vertical oven spit alternating with slices of the lamb fat - it melts downward and bastes the whole stack. Without it this is dry turkey breast.
Press hard so the stack is dense, and set a whole onion at the base to steady it.
Roast at 180C for about an hour and a half, turning every twenty minutes.
Raise to 230C for the last ten minutes to char the outside.
Carve from the outside inwards with a long knife and serve in laffa with tahini and pickles. Meat.

recipes.title: Grilled Entrecote
recipes.description: Coarse salt and fire. Kosher meat is already salted in koshering, so it behaves differently on coals - less salt, more drying.
instructions: Take the meat out of the fridge a full hour ahead. A cut cold in the middle burns outside before the centre warms.
Dry it thoroughly with paper towel. Koshered meat releases more liquid because of the salting, which is why it resists browning.
Salt lightly - koshering has already driven salt inside. A normal amount on top gives an oversalted steak.
Grill over hot coals 3-4 minutes a side without moving it, until the bars mark clearly.
Move to a cooler part of the grill, brush with oil, garlic and rosemary, and finish to 52-54C in the centre.
Rest eight minutes before cutting - cutting early empties the juices onto the board. Meat.

recipes.title: Arayes
recipes.description: Pita stuffed with ground meat and grilled over coals. The fat soaks inward and the bread crisps outside.
instructions: Mix the meat with squeezed grated onion, parsley, tomato paste, baharat, chilli and salt.
Halve each pita and open the pocket. Do not separate it into two discs - the hinge holds the filling in.
Spread a very thin layer of meat, about half a centimetre. A thick layer stays raw while the bread burns.
Press firmly to force the air out and brush both outer faces with olive oil.
Grill over medium coals 6-7 minutes a side with a light weight on top, until the meat browns at the edges.
Cut into triangles and serve with tahini and lemon. Meat.

recipes.title: Merguez Sausages
recipes.description: A red lamb sausage built on harissa. It came with North African immigrants and became a fixture at every Israeli barbecue.
instructions: Soak the casings in warm water for half an hour and rinse them through.
Mix the meat with the fat, harissa, spices, garlic and water, everything ice cold. Fat that has warmed smears and the sausage splits as it cooks.
Chill the mixture an hour, then fill the casings through a funnel without packing them to the limit.
Twist into 12cm links, alternating direction each time so they do not unwind.
Prick each one twice with a needle - otherwise steam bursts them on the fire.
Grill over medium coals 10-12 minutes, turning often. Meat.

recipes.title: Chicken Heart Skewers
recipes.description: On every Israeli grill menu and almost nowhere else. Eight minutes exactly, no more.
instructions: Trim the top of each heart and remove any clots. Rinse thoroughly in cold water until it runs clear.
Marinate an hour in oil, garlic, paprika and cumin. The lemon and salt join only fifteen minutes before grilling.
Thread tightly onto skewers, about eight hearts each.
Grill over scorching coals four minutes a side. An overcooked heart turns to rubber and there is no way back.
Check one: the inside should be pink-brown, not grey.
Scatter coriander, squeeze lemon over and serve at once. Meat.

recipes.title: Charred Aubergine
recipes.description: The parve dish that sits on the same coals as the meat. Skin burnt through, inside like cream.
instructions: Prick each aubergine in four places with a fork. A sealed one explodes on the coals.
Set them straight onto hot coals, no skewer, and turn every five minutes.
It is ready when it collapses under its own weight and the skin is black and brittle - about 20 minutes.
Split lengthways and serve in the skin, so the smoky flesh stays in its own dish.
Scatter coarse salt and pour tahini loosened with lemon and garlic straight in.
Add diced tomato, parsley and olive oil. Parve - it sits beside the meat without difficulty.

recipes.title: Whole Grilled Sea Bass
recipes.description: A Mediterranean fish with fins and scales, whole over the coals. The scales stay on - they are the shield against the fire.
instructions: Sea bass has fins and scales and is therefore kosher. Ask the fishmonger to gut it and leave the scales on.
Score three diagonal slashes on each side - the heat reaches inside and the fish cooks evenly.
Fill the cavity with lemon slices, garlic and parsley, and salt generously inside and out.
Oil the grill bars, not the fish, and heat them thoroughly first. A cold grate is why fish sticks and tears.
Grill eight minutes a side over medium coals and turn once only, using two spatulas.
Pour olive oil and lemon over and serve. Parve - fish counts as parve and may accompany any meal.

recipes.title: Ptitim
recipes.description: Invented in the fifties at Ben-Gurion's instruction as a rice substitute during austerity. Toasting them dry is the whole difference.
instructions: Fry chopped onion in the oil to a deep gold, about seven minutes.
Add the dry ptitim and toast them in the pan 3-4 minutes until they turn light brown and smell nutty. Without toasting they come out sticky.
Add the tomato paste and turmeric and stir half a minute.
Pour in boiling water - cold water halts the cooking and makes them absorb unevenly.
Cover and cook on low heat 12-15 minutes until all the liquid is absorbed.
Turn off, lay a towel between pot and lid for five minutes, and separate with a fork. Parve.

recipes.title: Chicken Schnitzel
recipes.description: It came from Vienna as veal and was rebuilt here on chicken breast, because veal was out of reach. Coarse crumbs, not fine ones.
instructions: Slice the breast thin and flatten between two sheets of plastic to an even half centimetre. An uneven slice stays raw in one place and burns in another.
Season the meat itself with salt, pepper and paprika, not only the coating.
Pass through flour, shake well, then beaten egg, then crumbs pressed on firmly.
Let them stand 15 minutes before frying. That is what stops the coating peeling off in the oil.
Fry in a centimetre of oil at 170C, three minutes a side, to golden.
Drain on a rack, not on paper - paper traps steam and softens the crust. Meat - no butter and no cheese.

recipes.title: Kebab in Tahini
recipes.description: Kebab baked under a layer of tahini. The tahini sets and browns while the meat cooks inside it.
instructions: Knead the meat with squeezed grated onion, parsley, baharat and salt to a sticky mixture.
Press into a tray in a layer a centimetre and a half thick and bake at 220C for ten minutes, until it browns and releases fat.
Pour off the fat that has gathered. Without this the tahini floats on it instead of baking onto the meat.
Make a thin tahini with lemon, water and salt - thinner than a normal sauce, because it thickens in the oven.
Pour it over in an even layer, scatter pine nuts and return to the oven for 20-25 minutes.
It is ready when the tahini takes brown patches and the edges bubble. Meat - tahini is sesame, not dairy.

recipes.title: Beef Patties in Tomato Sauce
recipes.description: Tuesday dinner. The patties go into the sauce raw and cook in it - that is what keeps them soft.
instructions: Soak the bread in water and squeeze it out. Soaked bread rather than dry crumbs is what gives a soft patty.
Knead briefly with the meat, egg, grated onion, paprika, salt and pepper. Long kneading tightens the protein and toughens them.
Shape into balls with wet hands and chill half an hour.
Make the sauce: fry onion, add the paste for a minute, then the crushed tomatoes, sugar, salt and paprika. Simmer ten minutes.
Lower the raw patties into the simmering sauce without frying them first. They release flavour into the sauce instead of sealing it in.
Cook covered on low heat for 40 minutes. Serve with rice or ptitim. Meat.

recipes.title: Kiosk Cheese Toast
recipes.description: White bread, yellow cheese, tomato and zaatar, in a press. The cheapest meal you can buy in Israel.
instructions: Butter the outer face of each slice - that is what browns in the press, not the inside.
Lay the cheese on the bottom slice in a double layer so it melts from both directions.
Dry the tomato slices on paper towel. A wet tomato turns the bread to sponge.
Scatter zaatar and pepper and add chopped olives.
Press in a hot sandwich press 5-8 minutes, until cheese escapes at the sides and caramelises on the iron.
Cut on the diagonal and serve with a pickle. Dairy - there is no meat in it in any form.

recipes.title: Tuna Salad
recipes.description: A tin of tuna, mayonnaise and onion. The meal waiting in every Israeli fridge, and parve, because tuna is fish.
instructions: Drain the tuna thoroughly and press it in a sieve. Oil left in the tin thins the mayonnaise and the salad collapses.
Flake it with a fork into strands rather than mashing it to paste.
Chop the red onion very fine and soak it a minute in lemon to soften it.
Dice the pickles small and chop the eggs roughly.
Mix everything with mayonnaise, dill, lemon, salt and pepper.
Chill half an hour before serving. Parve - fish and egg are not meat, and the mayonnaise contains no dairy.

recipes.title: Mushroom and Spring Onion Omelette
recipes.description: Supper for whoever did not get round to cooking. Medium-low heat - an omelette on high heat is a brown, tough one.
instructions: Sear sliced mushrooms in a hot pan without stirring until browned, about five minutes. Stirring early draws the water out of them.
Add chopped spring onion for half a minute only.
Beat the eggs with a spoon of water, salt and pepper. The water turns to steam and lifts the omelette.
Lower the heat, pour the eggs in and draw the edges inward with a spatula so the liquid runs out.
While the top is still slightly glossy, fold it in half. An omelette dry in the pan will be too dry on the plate.
Scatter parsley and serve with bread. Parve - an egg is neither meat nor dairy.

recipes.title: Rice with Toasted Noodles
recipes.description: The noodles are fried to a deep brown before the rice goes in. Without that step it is just rice with pasta in it.
instructions: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear and drain. Surplus starch is what glues the grains together.
Break the noodles into 2cm lengths.
Heat the oil in the pot and fry the noodles to a deep brown, 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly. They burn in a second.
Add the drained rice and stir a minute so every grain is coated in oil.
Pour in boiling water, salt and turmeric, bring to a boil once, then cover and drop to the lowest heat for 18 minutes.
Turn off and rest ten minutes without lifting the lid, then separate with a fork. Parve.

recipes.title: Courgette Pashtida
recipes.description: A kibbutz dining-hall institution: a vegetable, eggs, cheese and a tin. This version has no pastry and no fuss.
instructions: Grate the courgettes coarsely, salt them and leave in a colander for 20 minutes.
Squeeze them hard by hand. Unsqueezed courgette gives a wet pashtida, and it is the one mistake the oven cannot fix.
Fry chopped onion to gold and let it cool a little.
Beat the eggs and add the crumbled and grated cheeses, flour, baking powder, dill and pepper.
Fold in the courgettes and onion and pour into a greased tin.
Bake at 180C for about 45 minutes, until the centre is set and the top golden. Dairy - eaten hot or cold.

recipes.title: Fried Tilapia
recipes.description: The fish of the Sea of Galilee, fried whole in nothing but flour. The promenade restaurants in Tiberias do no more with it, and they are right.
instructions: Tilapia has fins and scales and is kosher. Scale it and dry it thoroughly.
Score two diagonal slashes on each side and salt inside and out for fifteen minutes.
Dry it again - salt draws water, and a wet fish spits in the oil instead of crisping.
Mix the flour, paprika and garlic powder and coat the fish thinly, shaking off the excess.
Shallow-fry at 180C, 6-7 minutes a side, to a golden crisp crust.
Drain on a rack, squeeze lemon over and scatter parsley. Parve.

recipes.title: Malabi
recipes.description: The street-stall dessert, in a plastic cup with pink syrup and peanuts. Cornflour, not gelatine.
instructions: Dissolve the cornflour in one cup of the cold liquid. Cornflour added to hot liquid forms lumps that never break down.
Heat the rest with the sugar to just below the boil.
Pour the cornflour mixture in in a thin stream, whisking constantly.
Cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until it thickens and coats a spoon. Do not let it boil - boiling breaks the set.
Off the heat add the rose water and pour into cups. Cover with cling film touching the surface so no skin forms.
Chill four hours, pour the syrup over and scatter peanuts, coconut and pistachios. Dairy.

recipes.title: Home-Made Halva
recipes.description: Sesame and sugar only - entirely parve, despite what the Hebrew name looks like. Syrup at exactly 118C.
instructions: The Hebrew name shares three letters with the word for milk, but there is no dairy of any kind in it - this is sesame, sugar and water. Fully parve.
Boil the sugar, water and lemon to exactly 118C on a sugar thermometer. Lower and the halva never sets; higher and it sets like glass.
Warm the tahini to 45C. Cold tahini splits from hot syrup immediately.

Pour the syrup into the tahini in a thin stream, stirring with a spatula and not a mixer - mechanical mixing destroys the fibrous structure, and that structure is exactly what gives halva its strands.
Stir for only 30-40 seconds, until streaks appear, then stop at once.
Transfer to a lined tin, scatter pistachios, and cool 24 hours before cutting. Parve.

recipes.title: Krembo
recipes.description: The sweet sold only in winter, which moves fifty million units a season. Meringue on a biscuit under a chocolate shell.
instructions: Cook the sugar, water and glucose to 121C. That is the temperature that stabilises a meringue; below it, it weeps within the hour.
Whip the whites to soft peaks, then pour the boiling syrup in a thin stream down the side of the bowl, not onto the whisk.
Keep whipping eight minutes until the bowl cools and the meringue is glossy and completely stable.
Pipe a tall peak onto each biscuit and freeze twenty minutes to set.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil and cool it to 32C - hot chocolate melts the meringue.
Dip each peak upside down and chill. Parve - the chocolate must be free of dairy.

recipes.title: Sufganiyot
recipes.description: Sweet yeast dough, deep fried and filled with jam. Deliberately parve, so they reach a meat Hanukkah table too.
instructions: The dough is built on orange juice instead of milk, which keeps the doughnut parve and lets it follow a meat meal.
Mix the yeast, sugar and warm juice and wait for foam.
Knead with the flour, eggs, oil and salt for ten minutes to a smooth, slightly tacky dough, and prove an hour and a half.
Roll to 1.5cm, cut rounds, and prove again for 45 minutes covered - the second prove is what creates the pale ring around the doughnut.
Fry at 165C only, a minute and a half a side. Oil any hotter burns the outside and leaves the middle raw.
Drain, fill with jam using a piping bag and nozzle, and dust with icing sugar. Parve.

recipes.title: Whole Orange Cake
recipes.description: The oil cake of every Israeli household. A whole orange - peel, juice and all - into the blender.
instructions: Wash one whole orange and cut it into quarters with the peel on, removing only the pips. Blend with the juice of the second orange.
The peel is the flavour. A cake made on juice alone comes out pale and sweet with no depth.
Whisk the eggs and sugar four minutes until pale and doubled in volume.
Add the oil in a thin stream, then the orange puree.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and fold with a spatula in as few strokes as possible. A mixer develops gluten and the cake turns rubbery.
Bake at 170C for 45-50 minutes until a skewer comes out dry. Dust with icing sugar once cool. Parve.

recipes.title: Tahini Cookies
recipes.description: Three basics and tahini in place of butter. They crumble in the mouth, and they are entirely parve.
instructions: Mix the tahini, sugar, oil, date syrup, vanilla and salt to a smooth paste.
Add the flour and mix only until the dough comes together. Over-kneaded dough gives a hard cookie instead of a crumbly one.
The dough will look dry and crumbly - that is correct. Pressed into a ball by hand it holds.
Roll walnut-sized balls, dip the tops in sesame and flatten slightly.
Bake at 170C for 13-15 minutes only. They stay pale - a browned cookie is a dry one.
Cool completely on the tray before moving them; warm, they fall apart between your fingers. Parve.

recipes.title: One-Bowl Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: One bowl, one spoon, no mixer. The boiling water at the end is what makes it moist.
instructions: Sift the flour, sugar, cocoa, soda and salt together into one bowl.
Add the oil, eggs and vinegar and stir with a spoon to a thick batter. The vinegar activates the soda, and that is what lifts the cake without baking powder.
Pour in the boiling water and stir. The batter will look far too thin - that is correct, and it is where the moisture comes from.
The hot water also blooms the cocoa, deepening both colour and flavour.
Pour into a greased tin and bake at 180C for about 40 minutes.
Cool in the tin twenty minutes before releasing. Parve - which is why it reaches a meat Shabbat table too.

recipes.title: Jerusalem Rugelach
recipes.description: Yeast dough, not cheese dough - the Jerusalem version, dipped in sugar syrup the moment it leaves the oven.
instructions: Knead a rich yeast dough with the margarine - not cheese, which is what separates Jerusalem rugelach from the American kind and what makes it parve.
Prove an hour, then chill the dough a further hour. Cold dough rolls thin without tearing.
Roll into a circle, spread with chocolate spread mixed with cocoa and sugar, and cut into 16 triangles.
Roll from the wide base towards the point and curve slightly. Prove 40 minutes.
Bake at 190C for 18-20 minutes to a deep brown.
Dip in boiling sugar syrup the instant they come out of the oven - a moment of waiting and they will not absorb it. Parve.

recipes.title: No-Bake Cheesecake
recipes.description: Israel's Shavuot cake - no oven, built on soft white cheese rather than American cream cheese.
instructions: Crush the biscuits, mix with the melted margarine and press into the base of a springform tin. Chill half an hour.
Sprinkle the gelatine over a quarter cup of cold water and leave five minutes to bloom, then melt it over steam. Never over direct heat - boiled gelatine loses its setting power.
Whip the cream to firm peaks and set aside.
Beat the cheese with the sugar and lemon, and add the warm gelatine in a thin stream while stirring fast.
Fold the whipped cream in gently and pour over the biscuit base.
Chill at least six hours, and only then spread the jam over the top. Dairy - the gelatine must be certified.

recipes.title: Limonana
recipes.description: Invented in a 1992 Israeli advertising campaign for a drink that did not exist - and within a year it was in every cafe in the Middle East.
instructions: Dissolve the sugar in a cup of hot water and cool completely. Undissolved sugar sinks to the bottom of the glass.
Blend the mint with the lemon juice and ice in short pulses. A blender left running heats the leaves and the drink comes out brown and bitter.
Add the syrup, water and salt and blend five seconds more.
Taste: if it is too sharp add syrup, not water - water dilutes the mint as well.
Serve at once in tall glasses. Limonana left standing ten minutes loses both its foam and its colour.
Garnish with mint leaves and lemon zest. Parve.
